Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
6 October 2026 .
Brent $ 99.45 -2.49 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 Iran claims whether Hormuz stays open or closed is tied to US fuel prices, not US presidential posts, per Iranian state media; Hellenic Shipping News reports Iraq's state-owned Oil Tanker Company moved 2 million barrels of Iraqi crude through the waterway using a very large crude carrier.

Situation
On the closure dispute, Iranian state media claim that whether the strait remains open or closed is a function of US fuel prices, not of US presidential statements; Hellenic Shipping News, separately, reports Iraq's state-owned Oil Tanker Company moved 2 million barrels of Iraqi crude through the waterway by very large crude carrier, a data point that sits in tension with a declared closure. Brent stood at $99.45, down 2.49% over 24 hours, as of 08:52 UTC. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Fifty-two events have been indexed in the past 24 hours. As of 08:50 UTC, 184 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
